meta.title: request handler panicked: cannot find `!BoundConst { var: 0 }`
meta.fix_ref: rust-lang/rust-analyzer#21235 (fix: resolve const generic param-env panic in type projection)
meta.build_notes: GitHub release asset rust-analyzer-aarch64-apple-darwin.gz of the weekly tags 2025-12-08 (0.3.2711, 5e3e9c4e61) and 2025-12-15 (0.3.2719, 87cf6631c6); the fix merged 2025-12-09. The fix passes the real ParamEnv to projected_ty in borrowck (mutability_of_locals, moved_out_of_ref, partially_moved), which the diagnostics use.
meta.notes: Bisected by the reporter to #20974. The panic surfaces as the error response -32603 'request handler panicked' to the request that computes the diagnostics of the file. Headless evidence (attempt 1): the panic is not history-dependent; a fresh session's first diagnostics request already panics, so the case is an error-response bug on a valid program rather than an R1 history bug (the reporter's editor presumably made its first diagnostics request before the crate had loaded).

settings_note: The reporter's settings (checkOnSave with clippy) are not needed: the panic is in the native diagnostics; the session keeps checkOnSave off.

files.source: issue body, code snippet to reproduce

files.note: a library crate around the snippet (package name, version, edition 2021)

repro.steps: The issue's literal steps and symptom: open src/lib.rs, let the server load the crate, make an edit (a whitespace change: insert a space on the blank line of f), then request the file's diagnostics (textDocument/diagnostic, the request the editor makes after an edit). Reported: the error -32603 'request handler panicked: cannot find !BoundConst { var: 0 } in param-env'. The session withholds the pull-diagnostics capability, so settling does not depend on the request under test.

attempts.summary: As screened (R1 edit-undo): insert and delete a space, then textDocument/diagnostic compared with fresh sessions on the same text. On 2025-12-08 the case session, the fresh session and the control session all answered -32603 'request handler panicked: cannot find !BoundConst { var: 0 } in param-env' (3/3 runs), so the answers were equal and the probe said absent; on 2025-12-15 all three answered a normal empty report. The panic does not depend on the edit history: in a headless client the first diagnostics request of a fresh session already panics.
